title: cross-sku-jitter-and-mixed-workload-scaling
content:
Purpose:
Run targeted cross-SKU experiments to quantify latency jitter and throughput variance under mixed inference workloads (short+long contexts, chat-like vs. embed/rerank) across A100 / H100 / L40S cloud SKUs and a small matrix of CUDA/driver versions.

Why this feels important now:
- We keep seeing intermittent p99 spikes in staging for multi-tenant traffic that mimic customer reports. Root cause is fuzzy: driver noise? kernel scheduling? NVLink vs PCIe locality?
- Prior benchmarks focused on single-model steady-state throughput; we need realistic mixed-run scenarios to surface jitter amplification and scheduling pathology.

Experiment summary (high level):
- Models: 1) tiny-chat (7B-ish, fp16), 2) long-context encoder-decoder (seq=4096), 3) embedding-only encoder (sequence 256), 4) reranker (pairwise short sequences).
- Workload mixes: A: 80% embeddings, 20% chat (many small requests); B: 50/25/15/10 mix (embedding/chat/long/rerank); C: 10% long, 90% chat bursts (tail-focused).
- SKUs tested: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100 40GB), GCP a2-highgpu-1g (A100 40GB), Azure ND96asr_v4 (A100), AWS p5.48xlarge (H100), GCP h2 (H100), Azure L40s offering (NVL40S equivalence).
- Driver/CUDA matrix: CUDA 11.8 + driver 535; CUDA 12.1 + driver 550; CUDA 12.2 + driver 555 (where available). Also a small test with older driver 510 on A100 for baseline.
- Load pattern: Poisson interarrival with occasional microbursts (100–300ms windows) simulated by our workload-replay tool. Batch packing enabled with timeout=10ms and max_batch_tokens tuned per model.
- Observability: per-request trace ids injected; collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, stddev(latency) over 1s windows (jitter), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, kernel occupancy, PCIe/NVLink counters, power draw, and nvprof timelines for selected traces.

Key results (high level findings):
1) Jitter amplification on H100 under mixed small-request workload: H100 SKUs showed lower median latency on long sequences but higher per-second stddev for chat-heavy mixes compared with A100. Spikes correlated with kernel preemption and context-switch-like gaps in nvprof traces.
2) L40S is stable for embedding-heavy traffic but shows elevated p99 when long-context jobs are concurrently scheduled on the same node. Likely memory bandwidth contention (observed sustained HBM utilization saturating).
3) Driver sensitivity: CUDA 12.2 / driver 555 reduced observed kernel launch tail times on H100 vs older 12.1/550 by ~12% in our sampled traces. A100 saw less dramatic improvements (<5%).
4) Burst arrival amplification: Microbursts push the batch-packing mechanism to flip between many tiny batches and a single large batch, causing alternating low and very high latencies (switching penalty ~20–60ms depending on model). This effect was most visible on SKUs with slower host-to-device PCIe (non-NVLink) variants.
5) NVLink vs PCIe locality: Instances with NVLink (multi-GPU) had fewer p99 tail spikes for long-context models, but inter-GPU interference still causes occasional throughput collapse when KV cache grows beyond local-GPU memory and cross-device transfers increase.

Interesting traces / evidence: (refer to linked artifacts for raw captures)
- nvprof trace (H100, CUDA12.1) showing alternating 3ms compute kernels then a 40ms gap where host-side scheduling requeues work (see PR #142 profiling helper).
- HBM utilization plots: L40S node with concurrent long+chat shows HBM pinned at 95% and p99 latency climb to 3x baseline.
- Kernel queue-length heatmap indicates preemption events align with bursts from separate tenant stream.

Immediate actions / mitigations to try (short term):
- Tune batch-packing timeouts per workload mix: increase timeout to 20ms for embedding-dominant routed queues, reduce to 5ms for chat-dominant flows; introduce adaptive timeout heuristic based on short-term arrival rate.
- Add a per-GPU scheduling isolation knob that pins long-context jobs to specific GPUs if KV cache propensity is detected (heuristic: >X bytes KV after warmup).
- Experiment with newer drivers on H100 fleet (12.2/555) in a canary to validate reduction in kernel tail times.
- Instrument our request router to prefer NVLink-local placement for long-context pairs when available.

Longer-term investigations (next quarter):
- Deep dive on kernel preemption behavior on H100: coordinate with low-level runtime team and vendor rep to get symbolized traces and possible microcode/driver fixes.
- Evaluate hybrid packing strategies that coalesce small requests across tenants with isolation bounds (safety checks for data privacy).
- Measure impact of quantization-induced additional kernel launches (int4/int8 paths) on jitter across SKUs. Hypothesis: more kernel launches -> more scheduling noise.
- Re-run experiments with more SKUs and cross-region network differences (GCP vs AWS host topology).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does H100 show larger stddev for small-request mixes even when median is better? Is there a preemption scheduler tuning we can control?
- How much of the PCIe-locality effect is from instance host topology vs cloud vendor firmware?
- Is the L40S HBM behavior reproducible at higher replication counts (we tested n=1–2), need larger sample sizes.

Notes for reproducibility (how we ran it):
- Workload driver: tools/workload-replay/mixed-runner.py --mix-file experiments/mixes/nov25-mix.json --arrive=poisson --burst-seed=20251103 --trace-sample-rate=0.01
- Runner deploy: infra/bench/deploy-runner.sh --sku ${SKU} --cuda ${CUDA_VER} --driver ${DRIVER_VER} --instance-count 1
- Profiling capture: profiler/capture.sh --trace-id $TRACE --nvprof --nvidia-smi-logging 1s --collect-hbm --collect-pcie
- Configs and raw results uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-bench/serving-runtime/cross-sku/2025-11-03/

Immediate TODOs (owners):
- Maya: spin up 12.2/555 canary on 2 H100 nodes, run Mix A and C, collect nvprof traces (due 2025-11-10).
- Ravi: implement adaptive batch timeout prototype in runtime (branch: runtime/adaptive-batching-jitter) and PR for review (JIRA-RT-824).
- Emilia: gather 10 additional L40S runs with varying long-model ratios to validate HBM hypothesis (due 2025-11-20).
- Noah: reach out to vendor rep (NV) with sample nvprof and kernel timelines asking about observed host-side gaps (slack thread linked).

Rough interpretation for product/CS:
Customers on H100 may see better median latencies for large models but intermittent spikes under chat-like noisy traffic. L40S is cost-efficient for embedding workloads but we need scheduling knobs before recommending it for mixed large-context deployments.

Attachments / where to find raw data: s3://redwood-bench/serving-runtime/cross-sku/2025-11-03/ and linked PR/JIRA above.

Questions for reviewers:
- Are we comfortable prioritizing adaptive timeouts before driver-wide canaries? (tradeoff: rollout time vs potential immediate improvement)
- Should we gate per-GPU pinning behind a config flag or make it default for long-context routes?

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- check whether host kernel preemption logs align with spike windows; might need dmesg / iostat on host too.
- consider using NVIDIA Nsight Systems next round for higher fidelity on preemption timing.

End of doc.
